# Relative Strength Index

A bounded momentum indicator over a price series. Take the period-over-period change, split it into
gains and losses, average each over a trailing window (14 periods by convention), and map the ratio
into 0–100:

```
RSI = 100 - 100 / (1 + AvgGain / AvgLoss)
```

High values mean recent moves were mostly upward, low values mostly downward. Conventional read
thresholds are 70 and 30 — but those are an *interpretation*, not part of the indicator, which is the
whole point of [[measure-vs-dimension]].

## Properties worth knowing before implementing

- **Bounded by construction.** The output cannot leave [0, 100]; that makes it easy to assert.
- **Warm-up.** With a 14-period window there is no defined value for the first 13 rows of a series.
  The implementation here writes `NULL` rather than a number derived from a short window, gated by a
  `COUNT(*)` over the same frame — see [[window-function-frames]].
- **Degenerate ends.** If average loss is zero the formula divides by zero; if average gain is zero
  the ratio is zero. Both are handled as explicit branches (→ 100 and → 0 respectively) rather than
  left to the arithmetic.
- **Two variants exist.** The simple moving average of gains and losses, and Wilder's original
  exponential smoothing. [[data-warehousing-and-business-intelligence]] implements the simple-average
  variant and **names Wilder's smoothing as the variant it did not implement** — an instance of
  [[provenance-and-limits-stated-inline]]. The two do not agree numerically, so an implementation that
  does not say which it is cannot be checked.

## Implemented twice

| | T-SQL | Python |
|---|---|---|
| Where | a four-CTE `UPDATE ... FROM` backfilling `RSI14` on the fact | `rsi_reference.py`, ~180 lines |
| Data | a staged real price extract (git-ignored) | a seeded random walk, stdlib only |
| Runs on | [[sql-server]] | [[sqlite]], no server |

The Python side exists to be runnable by anyone — see
{{reference-implementation-as-specification}} for what it does and does not verify. Its use of a
seeded random walk rather than a price file is deliberate: the three properties being checked
(warm-up length, boundedness, share of values inside the neutral band) hold for *any* series, so real
data would add nothing but a licensing problem. That is
[[dual-implementation-as-cross-check]] in intent, if not fully in execution.

## Where it is stored

On the fact table, as a measure, with the overbought/oversold flags derived in a view instead of
stored. See [[rsi-as-measure-not-dimension]] for the decision and its rejected alternative — which is
still in the tree.
